#tax #freelance

Threshold rose from £85,000 to **£90,000** on 1 April 2024; deregistration threshold £88,000. Test is rolling 12 months of taxable turnover, not the tax year, and you have 30 days from the end of the month you go over to tell HMRC. Rolling 12 months to 28 Feb 2025: £78,415, so £11,585 of headroom. The Wakefield housing association contract (PO WHA-20419, £1,450 a month from April 2025) would take me to about £89,800 by October, right at the edge. Options: decline extra work in the autumn, or register voluntarily. Most of my clients are small charities and sole traders who can't reclaim VAT, so adding 20% would cost them real money. Flat rate scheme for accountancy is 14.5% (13.5% in year one), which barely helps. Decision for now: watch it monthly on the Inputs tab of [[Budget spreadsheet]], invoice dates matter, and if a single invoice would push me over in the next 30 days alone that's the "forward look" test and I'd have to register straight away. Client reimbursed expenses are not turnover if handled as disbursements, which is why [[Expense policy]] wording on the Wakefield contract matters. Ask Graham at Lindley & Shaw what he did in 2022.
